about: What a bed and breakfast or small hotel may change in the Hearth design. Protected: the scroll-run townhouse cut open like a doll's house through one stay (arriving at dusk, checking in, up to your room, lights out, breakfast, out for the day) with the sky turning from dusk to night to morning, the drawn rooms, the calendar with nightly prices and minimum stays, the walking map, layout, type and all interaction code. The house's own words, its brick and door, the rooms with their colours and prices, the numbers, the sign at the corner, weekend prices and the places nearby come from the content.
rules: Text may not contain < > { } or line breaks.

house: the brick (red, brown, stone or white) and the door colour. The house shows five guest rooms: the first five rooms in rooms.list, in their colours (walls and throw). stay.room is the room you're shown up to in the hero (an index into rooms.list; the sixth shares the attic).
key: how many rooms, the check-in time, breakfast hours and minutes to town, and the four labels. sign: one or two places on the sign at the corner with their minutes. stay.clock: 24h or 12h.
stages: six steps in order: arriving at dusk, checking in, your room, lights out, breakfast, out for the day.
rooms.list: two to six rooms, each with a line, who it sleeps, the bed, its size, the nightly price and its colours.
dates: what a Friday or Saturday night adds, the fewest nights for a stay that includes one (1 to 3), and the words the calendar and request use.
nearby: three to six places with a line, minutes on foot and which way they lie (degrees from north), and the two rings drawn on the map (minutes).
